intervals.label: earlier ~10 kg Ge array announced
intervals.note: The official detector-suite page describes an earlier, smaller planned array; it is not clear from fetched sources whether this is the same physical array later reported as Ge-Mini (8 × 2.2 kg = 17.6 kg) in the 2024 evidence paper, or a distinct earlier generation. Recorded as a separate, lower-confidence interval rather than merged with the sourced Ge-Mini figures.
intervals.quote: A 10kg array of p-type point contact Ge detectors ... scheduled to be deployed later in 2020.

intervals.label: Ge-Mini operation, evidence of CEvNS on germanium
intervals.quote: deployed at the SNS and operated during the SNS neutron production period from June - August 2023

name: COHERENT germanium array (Ge-Mini)
notes: Mass conflict: the official detector-suite page (undated, accessed 2026) describes a planned 10 kg array for 2020; the 2024 evidence paper (arXiv:2406.13806) describes an 8 × 2.2 kg = 17.6 kg array (Ge-Mini) operated June-August 2023, of which 5-7 detectors were stable enough for analysis. specs.target_mass below uses the Ge-Mini figure, which is the one that actually produced the sourced physics result; the 10 kg figure is recorded only in the interval note above.

placements.quote: deployed at the SNS and operated during the SNS neutron production period from June - August 2023

module_count.note: 5-7 of the 8 detectors were stable enough to be used in the analysis at any given time.
module_count.quote: an array of eight 2.2 kg ICPC detectors

target_mass.note: Derived: 8 detectors x 2.2 kg = 17.6 kg, from the quoted "an array of eight 2.2 kg ICPC detectors". Total nominal array mass; not all 8 detectors were live throughout the run (see notes).
target_mass.quote: an array of eight 2.2 kg ICPC detectors

summary.plain: An array of eight ultra-pure germanium crystals, together weighing about 17.6 kilograms, that in 2024 became the third type of atomic nucleus on which COHERENT caught neutrinos bouncing off gently.
summary.technical: Ge-Mini: array of eight 2.2 kg inverted-coaxial point-contact (ICPC) high-purity germanium detectors, 1.5 keVee analysis threshold, operated at the SNS June-August 2023; yielded a 3.9σ rejection of the no-CEvNS hypothesis on natural germanium (2024).

technology.quote: The Ge-Mini detector of the COHERENT collaboration employs large-mass, low-noise, high-purity germanium spectrometers
technology.value: array of high-purity, p-type point-contact (inverted-coaxial) germanium spectrometers
